note: PG service bond and seat-leaving penalties for state-quota seats at government colleges, as written in each state's official counselling brochure. Private colleges generally do not impose a service bond.

states.service: Non-service candidates: 1 year Government service within 18 months of the PG degree. In-service candidates: 10 years
states.notes: In-service candidates' certificates are held by the sponsoring authority until the 10 years are served.
states.source: Dr NTR UHS PG (Competent Authority) prospectus 2025-26, §4.3 and §5

states.service: 3 years compulsory service under the State Government after the PG course
states.penalty: Leaving the course after admission: ₹15,00,000 plus all stipend received. Not serving the 3 years: ₹25,00,000 plus the salary received in that period
states.notes: Bond is signed at admission at government medical colleges; MBBS and PG certificates are held by the college until the service is done or the amount paid. Applies from session 2017-18 (corrigendum 26-04-2017).
states.source: Bihar Health Dept resolution 450(1) dt 15-04-2017 and corrigendum 479(1) dt 26-04-2017, Annexure 4 of the BCECEB PGMAC-2026 prospectus

states.service: No post-PG service bond in the admission procedure; seat-leaving bond only
states.penalty: Leaving the course midway: ₹10,00,000, the current year's fee plus 50% of next year's, and debarred from PG admission in Haryana for 3 years
states.notes: Applies to management seats too. ESIC Faridabad has its own bond.
states.source: Haryana Govt Gazette 185-2025, procedure for admission to MD/MS 2025, §12

states.service: Direct candidates: 2 years including 1 year field posting; in-service (GDO) candidates: 4 years (5 if sponsored outside the State)
states.penalty: As per the bond in the prospectus
states.notes: Applies to PG in Government Medical Colleges.
states.source: AMRU PG MD/MS/DNB Prospectus 2026, PG policy annexure

states.service: 1 year as Senior Resident in Kerala Medical Education Service immediately after the course (all general merit and AIQ candidates in Kerala)
states.penalty: Liquidated damages as per the bond
states.notes: Two bonds on ₹200 Kerala stamp paper at joining. Super-speciality: total bonded service up to 2 years.

states.service: Rural service bond and seat-leaving bond at admission (amounts set in the MP Medical Education Admission Rules 2018)
states.penalty: As per the Admission Rules; affidavit for upgrade on 0.5% of the bond amount
states.source: DME MP notice on PG bonds, 02-11-2026

states.service: 1 year social responsibility service (Govt of Maharashtra, local self-government or defence) after PG from a Government / Municipal Corporation college
states.notes: Private unaided colleges may not impose a bond or demand bank guarantees (circular 19-05-2018). In-service candidates: 1 year in a Government Medical College in addition to their DHS bond.
states.source: State CET Cell NEET-PG 2025 Information Brochure, §20.3–20.5

states.service: No post-PG service bond in the BFUHS prospectus (PCMS in-service candidates follow their service rules)
states.penalty: Security deposit to take part in Round 2 and later rounds: ₹25,000 (government colleges), ₹10,000 (SC/BC/PwBD, government colleges), ₹2,00,000 (private colleges, all quotas), forfeited under the government notifications
states.notes: The deposit is the counselling's seat-blocking safeguard, not a service bond.

states.service: 1 year in Government institutions, if required, after the course (non-in-service candidates)
states.penalty: Bond ₹20,00,000 (degree) / ₹10,00,000 (diploma); ₹50,00,000 for discontinuing after the free-exit date
states.notes: Training bond: complete the course or pay ₹50 lakh and refund stipend.
states.source: KNRUHS PG Competent Authority Quota prospectus 2024-25, §8

states.service: 2 years compulsory service in Uttar Pradesh after the PG course: as Senior Resident or contract lecturer in a government medical college, or as a contract specialist in a district hospital or CHC (outside the metro cities where possible)
states.penalty: ₹40,00,000 (MD/MS degree); ₹20,00,000 (PG diploma / MDS). Leaving the seat after the final counselling round, before finishing the course: debarred from the next academic session's admission (G.O. I/676928/2024 dt 26-06-2024)
states.notes: Applies to government medical and dental colleges. Resignation is accepted only as per G.O. I/1405837/2026 dt 23-07-2026.
states.source: DGME UP PG counselling brochure 2026, Chapter 8 (G.O. 950/71-2-82/2017 dt 07-03-2018 as amended)

states.service: 3 years (degree) / 2 years (diploma) to Govt of West Bengal after the course, open-category candidates
states.penalty: Leaving mid-course: ₹5,00,000 (degree) / ₹2,00,000 (diploma); not serving: penalty fixed by the State
states.notes: No discontinuation bond for DNB seats. In-service candidates follow TR rules.
states.source: WBMCC Notice cum Information Bulletin, WB PG Medical 2026
